A foreign key describes a reference from one table to another and can help prevent records from pointing to missing parents. In a workspace application, documents reference their workspace, while chunks reference their document. Authorization still needs to check which user owns the workspace. Maintaining indexes also consumes storage and adds work when rows change. Exact vector search compares the query vector against every eligible stored vector. This is a useful baseline because it returns the actual nearest neighbors under the chosen distance measure. Approximate vector indexes trade some retrieval recall for lower query latency. A telescope gathers light from distant objects. The observer chooses a location away from bright streetlights and allows their eyes to adapt to darkness. A larger aperture collects more light and can reveal dimmer objects. Magnification alone is not a measure of telescope quality because atmospheric turbulence and the instrument's optics also affect the image. The observer checks a star chart before going outside and records the date, approximate sky conditions, and equipment used. These notes make observations easier to compare across nights. An optical telescope collects visible light; a radio telescope detects radio waves. Both instruments investigate celestial objects but operate on different parts of the electromagnetic spectrum. A stable mount helps keep the target in view. Tracking becomes useful when the apparent motion of the sky would otherwise carry the target out of the field. A rechargeable battery stores energy through electrochemical reactions. During use, chemical processes support a flow of electric charge through an external circuit. A charger supplies energy to reverse suitable reactions in a rechargeable cell. The device manufacturer specifies the charging conditions and protective circuitry for a particular battery. Battery capacity describes how much charge a cell can deliver under specified conditions. It does not by itself determine how fast a device can charge. Temperature, internal resistance, and the charger also affect practical behavior. A technician records the load, ambient temperature, and test duration when comparing cells. Comparing numbers from tests with different conditions can be misleading. A battery management system monitors operating conditions and can limit charging or discharging. A puppy is a young dog. The words puppy and dog describe related animals even though their spellings are different. A shelter introduces a newly adopted animal to its home gradually. The handler prepares a quiet sleeping place, clean water, and a predictable routine before the animal arrives. Young animals can be nervous in unfamiliar rooms and should be allowed to explore without being forced into contact. Training uses rewards for desired behavior rather than punishment. A small food reward can follow a successful response to a cue. Short practice sessions are easier to repeat than long, exhausting drills. The trainer should reward the behavior immediately so the animal can associate its action with the reward. Consistency between family members matters because contradictory cues make learning harder. Puppies learn commands through short sessions with immediate positive rewards. This principle also applies when an older dog learns a new behavior.
